title: Gaussian torus Fourier approximation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $p$ satisfy $1\le p<\infty$, and let $m:(\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\})\to\mathbb Z$ be an integer frequency vector. The Fourier character on the product torus with frequency $m$, pulled back along the map sending $x\in\mathbb R^n$ to the torus coordinates $x_i$ and $\sqrt{2}x_i$ modulo $1$, belongs in Gaussian $L^p(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$ to the closure of the restrictions of complex polynomials.
hypotheses_covered: $m$ is an integer-valued frequency vector on the coordinate-and-bit index set
